import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Agents ask for a **capability** such as `reasoning-large`, not a vendor model. The control plane maps it to a concrete **Anthropic** or **OpenAI** model from the providers you have keyed. You swap a model, or ride out a provider outage, with no agent code change, and a cheap agent never fails over into an expensive model.

## Providers and keys

Two providers today:

- **Anthropic**: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku (defaults `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`; override with `PAL_OPUS_MODEL`, `PAL_SONNET_MODEL`, `PAL_HAIKU_MODEL`)
- **OpenAI**: `gpt-4o` and `gpt-4o-mini`

Add a key under **Settings** (LLM providers) or over the API:

```text
POST /v1/settings/llm-providers
{ "provider": "anthropic", "apiKey": "sk-ant-..." }
```

Keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest when `PAL_CREDENTIAL_KEY` is set (plaintext otherwise, so set it outside dev). They never appear in logs, traces or run state. The control plane resolves them per tenant at call time. Scored picks (`auto`, `cheap`, `best`) only consider providers you have keyed.

## Capability names

Use these strings in `model` fields. Resolution happens in the control plane (`llm_proxy.go`). Fixed names are pinned to one provider; the rest pick by which providers are keyed.

| Name | Resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| `reasoning-frontier` | Opus (`PAL_OPUS_MODEL`), always Anthropic |
| `reasoning-large`, `code-large` | Sonnet, always Anthropic |
| `reasoning-small` | Haiku, always Anthropic |
| `chat-large`, `vision-large` | `gpt-4o`, always OpenAI |
| `chat-small`, `vision-small` | `gpt-4o-mini`, always OpenAI |
| `chat-edge`, `code-small`, `cheap`, `fast` | Haiku if Anthropic is keyed, else `gpt-4o-mini` |
| `best` | Opus if Anthropic is keyed, else `gpt-4o` |
| `auto`, `balanced`, empty string | Scored pick among keyed providers ([How `auto` works](#how-auto-works)) |
| `embed-large`, `embed-small`, `rerank`, `transcribe`, `tts` | Not servable by text completion; routed to the same scored pick as `auto` |

"Anthropic keyed" means the tenant has an active Anthropic key or the process has `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Always-pinned names do not check which providers you keyed, so a pinned name whose provider has no key is left to [failover](#failover).

- **Unknown names** route to the balanced default, same as `auto`. The control plane logs one WARN per distinct name (capped at 256) and never routes an unknown to a hardcoded model.
- **Literal vendor names** pass through unchanged: `gpt*`, `o1*`, `o3*` go to OpenAI, `claude*` to Anthropic. The match is a plain prefix and the name is not validated; a wrong id fails at the provider. Prefer a capability.
- **`fast` and `cheap`** both map to the cheap tier. Neither optimizes for latency here; use `PAL_ROUTE_STRATEGY=fast` for that.
- **Which callers use this table:** workflow `ai-step` nodes. Session turns use complexity routing by default (each turn classified trivial, balanced or hard); set `PAL_COMPLEXITY_ROUTING=0` for plain `auto` scoring.

### How `auto` works

`auto` scores each model in a built-in catalog (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`) on quality, speed and cost and picks the top scorer among keyed providers. With neither provider keyed it returns `gpt-4o` and the call fails with a missing-key error.

`PAL_ROUTE_STRATEGY` changes the weighting for every name that resolves to the scored pick:

| Value | Picks |
| --- | --- |
| `balanced` (default) | Quality first, price as a real penalty: Sonnet, else `gpt-4o`. Pin `reasoning-frontier` or `best` if you want Opus |
| `cheap` | Haiku or `gpt-4o-mini` |
| `quality` | Opus, else `gpt-4o` |
| `fast` | Haiku, else `gpt-4o-mini` |

## Per-agent model

Runs, sessions and workflow `ai-step` nodes with no capability of their own try the agent's `model` first.

```text
POST  /v1/agents          { "name": "triage", "model": "fast" }
PATCH /v1/agents/triage   { "model": "reasoning-large" }    # "" or "auto" restores the default chain
GET   /v1/agents/triage   →  { ..., "model": "reasoning-large" }
```

| Allowed value | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Default | `""`, `auto` |
| Cost or speed target | `fast`, `cheap`, `balanced`, `best` |
| Capability | `reasoning-frontier`, `reasoning-large`, `reasoning-small`, `chat-large`, `chat-small`, `chat-edge`, `vision-large`, `vision-small`, `code-large`, `code-small` |
| Vendor model id | `gpt-*`, `o1*`, `o3*`, `claude-*` (lowercase, 100 characters or fewer) |

Anything else returns 400, including embedding, rerank and speech capabilities; the error never echoes the value. If the agent's provider is not keyed, the agent uses the default chain. An `ai-step` with its own capability keeps it; only `auto` nodes take the agent's model. The model that answered is recorded on the run's `llm:main` step.

## Failover

The control plane fails over through a ranked chain: each keyed provider's top model, then that provider's cheaper tier (a separate quota tier), then the next provider.

- **429, 402 and 5xx** move to the next candidate; a rate limit adds a backoff first.
- **Agent models go first.** An agent's model heads the chain. A cheap-tier agent (Haiku or `*-mini`) fails over only to the other provider's cheap tier, never to a Sonnet, `gpt-4o` or Opus class model. If both cheap tiers fail, the call fails instead of escalating the bill.
- **No mid-sentence swap.** In streaming, failover happens only while zero tokens have been emitted. After the first token an error surfaces as `message_error`, never a splice ([Streaming](/docs/runtime/streaming/)).

OpenAI and Anthropic calls carry an `Idempotency-Key` header: a one-way hash of run, step, attempt and the request body, with a per-provider suffix on failover targets. A backoff retry or crash replay dedups at the provider instead of double-billing. Ad-hoc `/v1/completions` calls without a run use a hash of provider, model and messages (`llm_idempotency.go`).

## Model-router service

A separate Rust model-router service exists (gRPC `:50053`, address `PAL_MODEL_ROUTER_ADDR`, default `model-router:50053`). The control plane routes plain completions through it only when `PAL_USE_MODEL_ROUTER=1` (also `true` or `on`). It is **off by default**, and any router error falls back to the direct path. Enable it on a non-critical tenant first.

The router has its own mapping. The control plane resolves a model with the table above, converts it back to a router capability, and the router picks the concrete model. A provider supports a capability only if it lists it exactly:

| Router capability | Anthropic | OpenAI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reasoning-frontier` | `claude-opus-4-6` | not supported |
| `reasoning-large` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `o3` |
| `reasoning-small` | `claude-haiku-4-5` | not supported |
| `code-large` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `gpt-4o` |
| `chat-large` | not supported | `gpt-4o` |
| `chat-small` | not supported | `gpt-4o-mini` |
| `embed-large`, `embed-small` | not supported | `text-embedding-3-large`, `text-embedding-3-small` |

`auto` and unspecified become `chat-large`. Among providers that support the capability, the optimize target orders them: cheap by price, fast by p50 latency, best by quality score, balanced by a fixed provider preference.

<Aside type="caution">
Router model ids are fixed in the service and not overridable by `PAL_OPUS_MODEL` and friends. With the router on, the Opus tier is `claude-opus-4-6`, not the control-plane default `claude-opus-4-8`.
</Aside>
